company.name: Hays plc
company.fiscalCalendar: Hays reports on a 30 June fiscal year-end; FY2026 is the financial year ended 30 June 2026, with quarterly trading updates and half-year results in February.

sources.title: Quarterly Trading Update for the Three Months Ended 30 June 2026
Preliminary Results for the Year Ended 30 June 2025
Half-Year Report for the Six Months Ended 31 December 2025

businessModel.claim: Hays is a specialist recruitment company that places candidates into permanent jobs and temporary/contract assignments, earning net fees (gross profit) on those placements across a global network of offices.

productsAndCustomers.claim: Hays serves employers and candidates through Permanent placement and Temp & Contracting recruitment, with its four largest specialisms being Technology, Accountancy & Finance, Engineering and Construction & Property, and a large Enterprise Solutions business for major clients.

segmentsAndGeographies.claim: Hays reports net fees across four regional segments: Germany, United Kingdom & Ireland (UK&I), Australia & New Zealand (ANZ) and Rest of World (RoW); as at 30 June 2026 it had c.8,100 employees in 155 offices in 23 countries and is refocusing on 16 core countries.

fiscalCalendar.claim: Hays' financial year ends 30 June; FY2026 is the year ended 30 June 2026, with full-year results scheduled for 20 August 2026 and quarterly trading updates in October, January, April and July.

revenueAndCostDrivers.claim: Net fees are driven by placement volumes, average fees/mix and, in Temp & Contracting, average hours worked; profit is driven by net fee levels, consultant productivity, consultant and non-consultant headcount and structural cost savings (c.£50m per annum secured in FY26).

accountingDefinitions.claim: Hays presents results on a pre-exceptional basis (excluding restructuring, impairment and transformation charges) and separately reports pre-exceptional operating profit and pre-exceptional basic EPS; net fees are turnover less the cost of sales (i.e. gross profit).

guidanceStyle.claim: Hays references company-compiled analyst consensus for its key profit metric and frames outlook against that range; for FY26 it stated pre-exceptional operating profit will be at the top of the £37.0-46.0m consensus range (company-compiled consensus of £43.5m based on 10 analysts).

cyclicalityAndSeasonality.claim: Recruitment net fees are highly cyclical and sensitive to labour-market conditions, with Temp & Contracting more resilient than Permanent through downturns; Hays expects near-term market conditions to remain challenging with greater resilience in Temp & Contracting than in Perm.

externalExposures.claim: Hays is exposed to heightened global macro-economic uncertainty and to currency movements versus sterling (notably the Euro and Australian Dollar), which materially affect reported net fees and operating profit.

signalMap.signal: Most recent reported full-year net fees as FY2026 starting range
signalMap.hypothesis: The last reported full-year net fees figure (£972.4m for FY2025), adjusted downward for the FY2026 like-for-like decline reported through Q4, is the strongest defensible starting range for FY2026 net fees pending the 20 August 2026 full-year results.
signalMap.freshnessRequirement: latest available reported figure before cutoff

signalMap.hypothesis: The last reported full-year pre-exceptional basic EPS (1.31p for FY2025) is the strongest defensible starting range for FY2026, consistent with FY2026 pre-exceptional operating profit guided broadly in line with to modestly above FY2025.
evidenceRequired: latest reported full-year pre-exceptional basic EPS
